subject: Deployment mode alignment: NimbleRetail latency & capacity clarifications
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@nimble.io>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode alignment: NimbleRetail latency & capacity clarifications

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the productive call earlier. I wanted to consolidate the notes and a short list of follow-ups so we can align on whether Hosted, Dedicated, or a Private deployment is the best fit for NimbleRetail.

Quick recap of what you shared:
- Target live traffic profile: baseline ~350 QPS, peak bursts up to ~600 QPS (short windows).
- Latency targets: p50 < 60ms, p99 target around 120–200ms depending on prompt size.
- Typical request size: 30–120 tokens; some batch scoring jobs at night with longer contexts.
- Data sensitivity: PCI-related workflows for checkout; most other paths are non-PII.

Two quick clarifying questions we need from you to finalize the recommendation:
1) Which traffic can be routed to a lower-trust environment (non-PII) where we could use Hosted as a cost-optimized fallback?
2) Any hard constraints on allowed downtime for rolling upgrades (SLA window) or maintenance?

Initial thoughts (to set expectations):
- Hosted API: fastest to launch and simplest. Good if the majority of traffic can tolerate multi-tenant routing and you want minimal ops. May meet p50 targets easily; p99 at your peak profile will depend on model choice and batching behavior.
- Dedicated capacity: best for predictable p99 latency and consistent tail behavior at scale. Recommended if bursts and p99 are business-critical (checkout flows).
- Private (VPC/on‑prem): required only if you must keep all requests on your network for compliance. This brings additional delivery time and ops overhead.

Attachments: I’m including a short deployment questionnaire and a pilot-plan template to capture the key signals (traffic windows, model candidates, success criteria). If you can fill the questionnaire it will let our engineers size a Dedicated pilot or validate Hosted fallback routing.

Proposed next steps:
- Samantha: share answers to the two clarifying questions + the questionnaire by EOD Tue (May 24) if possible.
- We’ll produce a short sizing estimate and two recommended pilot scopes (Hosted-first with Dedicated fallback vs Dedicated-only) for you to review.
- Schedule a 30-minute follow-up with Priyom (solutions) and Rishi (sales engineering) to walk through the pilot plan.

Available times: Mon/Tue mornings PST or Wed afternoon PST — what works best for Jason?

Thanks —

Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: nimble_deploy_questionnaire.pdf, pilot_plan_template.xlsx

From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@nimble.io>

Cc: Jason Park <jason.park@nimble.io>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode alignment: NimbleRetail latency & capacity clarifications

Laura —

Appreciate the concise recap. Quick answers inline:
1) Non-PII fallback: ~65% of realtime traffic can be considered non-PII and could be routed to a lower-trust environment. Checkout and payment validation (~35%) must stay in a high-trust environment.
2) Downtime constraints: we need rolling upgrades with no more than 5 minutes of degraded capacity for checkout flows; full outage is not acceptable.

For context, our infra lead Jason (cc’d) prefers Dedicated to avoid surprise tail latency during big shopping events. He’s worried about p99 on multi-tenant Hosted during peaks.

What we need from Redwood:
- A ballpark monthly cost range for a Dedicated pool sized for baseline 350 QPS and peak 600 QPS, and an estimated lead time to stand up the Dedicated environment.
- A pilot plan that proves p99 under the expected burst patterns.

We can fill out the questionnaire by Tue EOD. Also open to a Hosted-first pilot that routes checkout traffic to Dedicated, but we’d like clear fallbacks.

Thanks —

Samantha Ortiz
Head of Product, NimbleRetail
samantha.ortiz@nimble.io
+1 (617) 555-4502

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Deployment mode alignment: NimbleRetail latency & capacity clarifications

Hi Samantha / Laura —

Thanks for the quick turnaround — below are concrete sizing and pilot suggestions based on the profile you shared. I’ll keep this focused and technical so you can share with Jason.

Sizing assumptions (ballpark):
- Baseline 350 sustained QPS, peak bursts 600 QPS (short window, <5 minutes).
- Median request cost ~0.75k token ops per request (small model family); occasional longer context jobs at night.

Dedicated recommendation:
- Pilot pool: 4 x A100 GPUs (or 6 x H100 LLM-optimized instances if available) with a single-model pin to reduce cold-start variance. This configuration should comfortably handle baseline load with headroom for bursts when combined with autoscale.
- Autoscaling: aggressive scale-up policy with warm-standby nodes and pre-warming on scheduled events (e.g., promo starts).
- Expected p50: ~30–50ms; p99: depends on model and batching but we target <200ms with the above.

Hosted-first hybrid (alternate approach):
- Route non-PII (~65%) to Hosted API to reduce cost. Route checkout/payment flows to Dedicated pool via smart routing.
- Use prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts (checkout validation) to reduce cost and tail latency.

Operational constraints:
- For rolling upgrades, we recommend an at-capacity canary with automatic fallback. For checkout flows we can enforce a stricter canary policy with a 10-minute hold window before traffic migration.

Deliverables if you go Dedicated pilot:
1) Sizing estimate (attached as sizing_estimate.csv).
2) Pilot runbook (we’ll adapt your pilot_plan_template.xlsx).
3) Success criteria: p50 < 60ms, p99 < 200ms for checkout endpoints during a synthetic burst of 600 QPS sustained for 3 minutes.

Lead times: Dedicated pool (no special procurement) — ~2–3 weeks to provision and validate; Private/VPC has additional delivery overhead (~6–8 weeks) depending on approvals.

I’ll follow up with a short costs worksheet for the Dedicated pilot. If you want, we can provision a small Dedicated sandbox for a 2-week proof that focuses only on checkout traffic.

Regards,

Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: sizing_estimate.csv
